**(B)** Decay

The chapter lists the basic principles of life: metabolism (breaking and making of molecules), growth and development from within, and reproduction to continue the race. Decay is the breakdown of a body after death, so it is not a property of a living being. Metabolism, growth and reproduction are all named in the chapter as features of life.

**(A)** Herbarium

A strictly seasonal plant is available alive for only part of the year. A herbarium sheet is a dried, pressed and mounted specimen with its label (date, place, classification, characters), so it can be studied in the laboratory in any season. A botanical garden grows living plants in the field, and a flower exhibition is neither permanent nor scientific; a museum mainly keeps preserved specimens in jars and stuffed animals.

**(C)** Irritability

The chapter calls responsiveness, or irritability, a unique property of living beings: a living organism responds to changes in its surroundings. The students can touch or prod the cockroaches and see whether they react. Metabolism and growth cannot be seen at a glance, and reproduction cannot settle the question because sterile living beings such as mules and worker bees do not reproduce either.
